newsitem.title: CHINA: HK court awards man US$3 mln for injury claim.
newsitem.headline: HK court awards man US$3 mln for injury claim.

text.p: A Hong Kong court has awarded an American man HK$23 million (US$2.97 million) for a personal injury claim, his lawyer said on Thursday.
Kristan Phillips, 47, was awarded the sum, including interest, against five defendants including the local subsidiary of Swiss chemical giant Ciba-Geigy, his lawyer said in a statement.

The former principal timpanist with the Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra sued the defendants for negligence in allowing him to be poisoned during a pest control operation when he was rehearsing in June 1987.
The defendants also included the Orchestra and the Academy for Performing Arts, where the rehearsal took place.
The court found that nobody at the Academy tried to stop either the rehearsal or the pest control operation unitl it was too late.
It also decided that Ciba-Geigy (Hong Kong) Ltd, as importer of the pest control chemical, had failed to properly label containers to warn of the dangers in its use.

Phillips, who used to live in Hong Kong before moving back to the United States, then suffered from damage in his nervous system. The court found the damage could have stemmed from a single assault by the chemical, his lawyer said.
The victim has been declared mentally incompetent and uanble to manage his own afairs, and cannot work any more, the lawyer said.
